title: Attackers Use LLM Agent for Post-Exploitation After Marimo CVE-2026-39987 Exploit

reading.body:
An attacker used an AI agent to conduct a cyberattack following exploitation of a vulnerability in marimo notebook software. The agent made decisions in real time during post-exploitation, moving from initial access through credential theft to database exfiltration in less than one hour. The agent made assumptions about database structure without prior reconnaissance, formatted commands for machine processing, and chained outputs from one command into inputs for the next, all while routing through multiple IP addresses to avoid detection.

This represents a failure in the deployment of an AI system: an agent was given access to exploit tools and cloud environments without human oversight or approval gates between stages of attack. The attacker was able to direct the agent to accomplish a multi-stage intrusion that would normally require human decision-making. Detection of the intrusion occurred only after the attack was complete.

It is not established whether the AI agent was given explicit instructions for each attack stage or whether it autonomously selected tactics, or what safeguards, if any, were present to restrict the agent's access or actions during the operation.

reports.title: AI agent at the wheel: How an attacker used LLMs to move from a CVE to an internal database in 4 pivots
AI Agent Conducted a Cyberattack on Its Own — It Took Less Than One Hour
Attackers Use LLM Agent for Post-Exploitation After Marimo CVE-2026-39987 Exploit

summary:
# Summary

On May 10, 2026, the Sysdig Threat Research Team detected an intrusion where an artificial intelligence agent controlled by an attacker executed a sophisticated cyber attack in real time. The attacker exploited a vulnerability in marimo notebook software to gain initial access, extracted cloud credentials, and used Amazon Web Services to retrieve an SSH private key. The attacker then accessed an internal database server through an SSH connection. The entire attack from initial compromise to database theft took less than one hour, with the database exfiltration phase completing in under two minutes. The attacker routed activities through eleven different Cloudflare Workers IP addresses to avoid detection based on single source addresses.

The attack demonstrated four key characteristics that indicated an AI agent was making decisions during the intrusion rather than executing a pre-written script. The attacker made assumptions about database structure without prior knowledge, left planning comments in the command stream, formatted all commands for machine processing rather than human use, and extracted values from previous command outputs to use in subsequent actions. Sysdig recommended that organizations immediately update marimo software, audit credentials on exposed instances, rotate compromised access keys, and implement runtime threat detection across their networks.
